tools.name: list_accounts
tools.description: Lists the email accounts this connection can access through FGAC. account_details reports each account's Google scope state: gmail and drive_file are 'granted', 'missing', or 'unknown' ('unknown' means the state could not be determined right now — treat the account as usable and let a real call settle it; never treat 'unknown' as missing). A 'missing' scope means every call needing it will fail until the account is reconnected — the entry's reconnect_url is a one-click fix link to give the user; it is bound to that specific account, so the user must open it while signed in to FGAC as that account. google_token: 'unavailable' with a reconnect_url means the Google grant itself is dead (revoked, expired, or missing) — every call on that account fails until the user opens the link; do not retry, and read next_steps.reconnect first.

tools.name: gmail_list
tools.description: Search or list Gmail messages: returns recent message IDs, optionally filtered by a Gmail search query (e.g. "is:unread", "from:alice newer_than:7d") — this is the Gmail search tool; read a result with gmail_read. Works across every connected or delegated Gmail inbox — pass the "account" parameter to target a specific mailbox (see list_accounts). Other Gmail read endpoints (threads, drafts, history, settings) are available via google_api_get.

account.description: Email account to use. Defaults to primary.

max.description: Max messages to return (Gmail maxResults; default: 10). The parameter is named max.

tools.name: gmail_read
tools.description: Read a Gmail message by ID — arguments: messageId (required; the "id" from gmail_list), account, format, offset, limit. Returns parsed headers, body text, and attachment metadata. Reading is allowed by default; messages matching the user's read-block rules (labels or content patterns), if any, are withheld. Works across every connected or delegated Gmail inbox via the "account" parameter. For a full thread use google_api_get with gmail/v1/users/me/threads/{id}. Long messages: pass offset and a limit sized to your tool-result budget (chars, max 200000/call) to window the serialized message with the body UNtruncated — the envelope reports total_chars and next_offset; concatenate data strings in offset order.

account.description: Email account to use (see list_accounts; defaults to the primary). Ids are mailbox-specific: an id obtained on one account must be read with that same account passed here.

format.description: Response format, lowercase: "full" (default) returns parsed headers, body text, and attachment metadata; "metadata" and "minimal" are the Gmail API equivalents.

limit.description: Max chars to return in this response (server caps at 200000). Size this to YOUR tool-result budget. Passing offset or limit switches to the windowed envelope.

messageId.description: Gmail message ID — the "id" of an entry returned by gmail_list (not the threadId). The parameter is named messageId.

offset.description: Start position (chars into the serialized response, body UNtruncated) for a windowed read of a long message. Use the next_offset from the previous response to continue; start at 0.

tools.name: gmail_get_attachment
tools.description: Retrieve an email attachment by message ID plus either attachment ID or filename (allowed unless the parent message matches a read-block rule). Gmail attachment ids go stale when a message is re-indexed — stale ids are healed automatically when unambiguous, and filenames never go stale. Returns Gmail's base64url-encoded data (URL-safe alphabet, padded with "=") — decode with a base64url decoder, not standard base64. Files over ~150 KB must be read in windows: pass offset and a limit sized to YOUR tool-result budget (chars of base64url data, max 200000/call); each response reports total_chars and next_offset — concatenate the data strings in offset order, then decode once. Over ~1 MB, if you can run code with network access, create_temporary_api_key downloads it in one request instead.

account.description: Email account to use (see list_accounts; defaults to the primary).

attachmentId.description: Attachment ID, taken from the `attachments` array of a gmail_read on THIS messageId. Prefer `filename` when you know it — filenames never go stale.

filename.description: Attachment filename as shown in gmail_read `attachments` (case-insensitive), as an alternative to attachmentId.

limit.description: Max chars of base64url data to return in this response (server caps at 200000). Passing offset or limit switches to the windowed envelope.

messageId.description: Gmail message ID containing the attachment

offset.description: Start position (chars into the base64url data) for a windowed read of a large attachment. Start at 0.

tools.name: gmail_send
tools.description: Send a plain-text email from any connected or delegated account (via the "account" parameter). Recipients must match the user's FGAC send whitelist; denied sends include a link the user can use to approve the recipient. The body is plain text; FGAC adds an HTML alternative generated from it (paragraphs, line breaks and links kept) because Gmail re-wraps text-only mail at ~72 columns on delivery. For your own HTML, attachments, or threaded replies, use google_api_modify with Gmail messages/send and a raw RFC 2822 MIME body; the same whitelist applies. Attachments over ~1 MB: use create_temporary_api_key and Gmail's resumable messages/send upload from a script.

tools.name: sheets_get_spreadsheet
tools.description: Get metadata and sheet tabs for a Google Spreadsheet exposed by the user's FGAC rules — arguments: spreadsheetId (required), account, offset, limit. Large responses: pass offset and a limit sized to your tool-result budget (chars, max 200000/call) — the windowed envelope reports total_chars and next_offset; concatenate data strings in offset order.

spreadsheetId.description: Google Spreadsheet ID (e.g. 1BxiMVs0...) — the segment after /d/ in the sheet URL; a full URL is accepted and the id extracted

tools.name: sheets_read_range
tools.description: Read cell values from a sheet tab or range in a Google Spreadsheet exposed by the user's FGAC rules — arguments: spreadsheetId and range (both required), account, offset, limit. Prefer narrowing the range; for genuinely large ranges, pass offset and a limit sized to your tool-result budget (chars, max 200000/call) — the windowed envelope reports total_chars and next_offset; concatenate data strings in offset order.

range.description: A1 range: 'Tab name'!A1:D20 (single quotes around a tab name with spaces), or a bare tab name for the whole tab. Tab names must match an existing tab exactly — take them from sheets_get_spreadsheet rather than assuming 'Sheet1'.

tools.name: slides_get_presentation
tools.description: Read a Google Slides presentation exposed by the user's FGAC rules. Returns the raw Slides API presentation resource (title, slides, page elements with their text and shapes as structured JSON). Large decks: trim with the optional "fields" mask (e.g. "title,slides(objectId,pageElements(shape(text)))"), or read in windows by passing offset and a limit. To edit the presentation use slides_edit; comments live in the Drive API — use comments_read.

fields.description: Optional Slides API field mask to trim the response.

presentationId.description: Google Slides presentation ID — the segment after /d/ in the presentation URL; a full URL is accepted and the id extracted

tools.name: slides_edit
tools.description: Apply Google Slides batchUpdate requests to edit presentations — add or delete slides, create shapes, text boxes, images and tables, insert/replace/delete text, restyle text and shapes (https://developers.google.com/slides/api/reference/rest/v1/presentations/batchUpdate). Examples: add a blank slide {"createSlide":{"slideLayoutReference":{"predefinedLayout":"BLANK"}}}, replace text everywhere {"replaceAllText":{"containsText":{"text":"old","matchCase":true},"replaceText":"new"}}, or insert text into a shape {"insertText":{"objectId":"<shapeId>","text":"..."}} (object ids come from slides_get_presentation). Requires Read & Write FGAC access. Create new presentations with google_api_modify (POST v1/presentations).

requests.description: Slides API batchUpdate request objects, applied in order (e.g. createSlide, createShape, insertText, deleteText, replaceAllText, createImage, updateTextStyle, deleteObject)

tools.name: google_api_get
tools.description: Perform a read-only GET request against any Google API endpoint by path — the full read surface behind the typed convenience tools. Gmail: messages, threads, drafts, labels, history, settings — reads are allowed by default and filtered by the user's read-block rules if any. Google Sheets, Google Docs, and Google Slides: require a per-file FGAC rule. Drive: listing (drive/v3/files) is never gated; any call addressed to a file by id (metadata, export, revisions, permissions, comments) follows that file's FGAC rule. APIs outside the grant — People/Contacts, Calendar, Tasks, YouTube — can NEVER work through FGAC and are refused; do not probe them. Batch endpoints are denied. Use this whenever no typed read tool covers the endpoint you need.

account.description: Email account to use (see list_accounts; defaults to the primary).

tools.name: request_access
tools.description: Ask the user to grant this agent a specific permission: sending email to a recipient, or read/write access to a Google Spreadsheet, Google Docs document, or Google Slides presentation. Arguments: type (required — one of send, sheets_read, sheets_write, docs_read, docs_write, slides_read, slides_write) plus recipient for send, or spreadsheetId / documentId / presentationId for a file. Returns a permanent approval link for the user — calling this tool grants nothing by itself; the user must open the link and approve. For a spreadsheet, document, or presentation, pass resourceName (the file's title) whenever you know it: the approval page shows it, and without it the user only sees Google's file id while Google's picker lists files by name.

documentId.description: Google Docs document ID (required for docs types)

presentationId.description: Google Slides presentation ID (required for slides types)

recipient.description: Email address to whitelist (required for type "send")

resourceName.description: Title of the spreadsheet, document, or presentation, when you know it. Shown on the approval page so the user can find the file by name in Google's picker.

spreadsheetId.description: Google Spreadsheet ID (required for sheets types)

tools.name: create_temporary_api_key
tools.description: Create a short-lived FGAC API key so code YOU run can move data too large for tool calls: file uploads to Drive, emails with large attachments, Drive downloads or Gmail attachments over ~1 MB, or many calls in a loop. The key has exactly this connection's permissions, enforced by the same FGAC rules on every request; it is not a Google token. Requires code execution with network access to the returned base_url; without it, keep using the windowed tools (gmail_get_attachment offset/limit) and google_api_modify. Lifetime: ttl_minutes, default 15, maximum 60. purpose (upload, download, send_attachment, bulk_calls, other) selects the step-by-step recipe returned with the key. Keep the key out of anything that leaves this session.

expected_bytes.description: Approximate size of the file or payload, if known.

purpose.description: What the script will do. Selects the recipe returned with the key. Default other.

annotations.title: Get a short-lived API key for scripts

tools.name: get_my_permissions
tools.description: Shows the access rules, accessible accounts, proxy key, and default access posture (including implicit Gmail read access) that apply to this connection.
